title: Isaiah Chapter 37 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 37 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 37 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 37.

questions.question: What did King Hezekiah do when he heard the news?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah rent his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD when he heard the news, as stated in Isaiah 37:1.

questions.question: Who did Hezekiah send to Isaiah the prophet?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah sent Eliakim, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, along with the elders of the priests to Isaiah, as mentioned in Isaiah 37:2.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah say was the situation on that day?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah described the day as a day of trouble, rebuke, and blasphemy in Isaiah 37:3.

questions.question: What did Isaiah tell Hezekiah's servants not to be afraid of?
questions.explanation: Isaiah instructed them not to be afraid of the words that the servants of the king of Assyria had blasphemed against God, as stated in Isaiah 37:6.

questions.question: What did the LORD promise to do to the king of Assyria?
options: Cause him to fall by the sword in his own land
questions.correctAnswer: Cause him to fall by the sword in his own land
questions.explanation: The LORD promised to send a blast upon him and cause him to fall by the sword in his own land, as noted in Isaiah 37:7.

questions.question: True or False: Hezekiah received a letter from Sennacherib.
questions.explanation: Hezekiah received a letter from the messengers, which he read before going to the house of the LORD, as mentioned in Isaiah 37:14.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah do with the letter he received?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah went up to the house of the LORD and spread the letter before the LORD, as stated in Isaiah 37:14.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah ask the LORD to do?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah prayed to the LORD asking to save them from Sennacherib's hand, as mentioned in Isaiah 37:20.

questions.question: True or False: The Assyrians had previously destroyed all nations and their countries.
questions.explanation: Hezekiah acknowledged that the kings of Assyria had laid waste to all nations and their countries, as stated in Isaiah 37:18.

questions.question: What did the gods of the nations represent according to Hezekiah?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah stated that the gods of the nations were not gods but the work of men's hands, wood and stone, as mentioned in Isaiah 37:19.

questions.question: Who was the king of Ethiopia mentioned in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Tirhakah is mentioned as the king of Ethiopia who was said to be coming forth to make war, as stated in Isaiah 37:9.

questions.question: True or False: Rabshakeh claimed that Jerusalem would not fall into the hands of the Assyrians.
questions.explanation: Rabshakeh sent a message stating to Hezekiah that Jerusalem would indeed fall into the hands of the king of Assyria, as implied in Isaiah 37:10.

questions.question: What assurance did the LORD give about the king of Assyria's attack?
options: He shall not come into this city
questions.correctAnswer: He shall not come into this city
questions.explanation: The LORD assured that the king of Assyria shall not come into the city, nor shoot an arrow there, as stated in Isaiah 37:33.

questions.question: In Isaiah 37, which instruction comes FIRST?
questions.explanation: The first action in Isaiah 37 is when Hezekiah heard the news, rent his clothes, and covered himself with sackcloth, as recorded in Isaiah 37:1.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 37 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 37 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah do when he heard the words of Rabshakeh?
options: He rent his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth
questions.correctAnswer: He rent his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth
questions.explanation: Hezekiah rent his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth as a sign of mourning and desperation, showing his deep concern and humility before God (Isaiah 37:1).

questions.question: Who did Hezekiah send to Isaiah the prophet?
options: Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests
questions.correctAnswer: Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests
questions.explanation: Hezekiah sent Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests to Isaiah to seek guidance and prayer regarding the threat from Assyria (Isaiah 37:2).

questions.question: What did Hezekiah's messengers tell Isaiah about their situation?
options: It is a day of victory
It is a day of trouble and rebuke
It is a day of celebration
It is a day of peace
questions.correctAnswer: It is a day of trouble and rebuke
questions.explanation: The messengers conveyed to Isaiah that it was a day of trouble, rebuke, and blasphemy, indicating the gravity of their circumstances (Isaiah 37:3).

questions.question: What does Isaiah instruct Hezekiah not to be afraid of?
options: The words of the king of Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: The words of the king of Assyria
questions.explanation: Isaiah reassured Hezekiah not to be afraid of the blasphemous words spoken by the servants of the king of Assyria (Isaiah 37:6).

questions.question: What promise does the LORD make regarding the king of Assyria?
options: He will send a blast upon him
questions.correctAnswer: He will send a blast upon him
questions.explanation: The LORD promises to send a blast upon the king of Assyria, causing him to hear a rumor that leads to his defeat (Isaiah 37:7).

questions.question: What was Hezekiah's immediate response after receiving the letter from Rabshakeh?
options: He spread it before the LORD
He called for a national fast
questions.correctAnswer: He spread it before the LORD
questions.explanation: Hezekiah went to the house of the LORD and spread the letter before God as a sign of seeking divine intervention (Isaiah 37:14).

questions.question: In his prayer, how does Hezekiah acknowledge God's sovereignty?
options: He states God is the only God of all kingdoms
questions.correctAnswer: He states God is the only God of all kingdoms
questions.explanation: Hezekiah recognizes God's sovereignty by declaring Him as the God of all kingdoms and creator of heaven and earth (Isaiah 37:16).

questions.question: What does Hezekiah ask the LORD to do in his prayer?
options: To save them from Sennacherib's hand
questions.correctAnswer: To save them from Sennacherib's hand
questions.explanation: Hezekiah pleads with the LORD to save them from the hand of Sennacherib so that all kingdoms may know that the LORD is God (Isaiah 37:20).

questions.question: What is the response of the LORD to Hezekiah's prayer?
options: He will save Jerusalem for His own sake
questions.correctAnswer: He will save Jerusalem for His own sake
questions.explanation: The LORD promises to defend and save the city of Jerusalem for His own sake and for the sake of His servant David (Isaiah 37:35).

questions.question: What does the verse Isaiah 37:36 reveal about the outcome of the Assyrian army?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the angel of the LORD struck down 185,000 Assyrians, and when the people woke up, they found them all dead (Isaiah 37:36).

questions.question: Sennacherib king of Assyria was ultimately killed by whom?
questions.explanation: Sennacherib was killed by his own sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer, while he was worshipping in the house of his god (Isaiah 37:38).

questions.question: Hezekiah's prayer demonstrates which biblical virtue?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's prayer shows his faith as he approaches God with his fears, seeking divine help and acknowledging God's sovereignty (Isaiah 37:15-20).

questions.question: The statement 'the virgin, the daughter of Zion, hath despised thee' refers to what?
questions.explanation: This statement refers to how the people of Jerusalem, represented as the daughter of Zion, scorn the Assyrian king for his blasphemy against God (Isaiah 37:22).

questions.question: Hezekiah did not believe that God could save Jerusalem from Sennacherib's hand.
questions.explanation: Hezekiah expressed his faith in God's ability to save Jerusalem when he prayed, demonstrating his trust in God despite the dire circumstances (Isaiah 37:20).

questions.question: The gods of the nations were powerful enough to save their people from the Assyrians.
questions.explanation: Hezekiah notes that the gods of the nations were not real and were destroyed, highlighting the powerlessness of idols compared to the living God (Isaiah 37:19).

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 37 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 37.

questions.question: What did King Hezekiah do when he heard the words of Rabshakeh?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah rent his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD when he heard the troubling news (Isaiah 37:1).

questions.question: Who did Hezekiah send to Isaiah the prophet?
options: Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests
questions.correctAnswer: Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests
questions.explanation: Hezekiah sent Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests to Isaiah (Isaiah 37:2).

questions.question: What message did Hezekiah convey to Isaiah regarding the situation?
options: It is a day of peace
It is a day of trouble, rebuke, and blasphemy
It is a day of victory
It is a day of preparation for war
questions.correctAnswer: It is a day of trouble, rebuke, and blasphemy
questions.explanation: Hezekiah described the day as one of trouble, rebuke, and blasphemy because of the threats from Assyria (Isaiah 37:3).

questions.question: What did Isaiah reassure Hezekiah about the Assyrians?
options: He should not be afraid of their words
questions.correctAnswer: He should not be afraid of their words
questions.explanation: Isaiah told Hezekiah not to be afraid of the blasphemous words spoken by the Assyrians (Isaiah 37:6).

questions.question: What would happen to the Assyrian king according to God's promise?
options: He would die by the sword in his own land
He would become a servant of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: He would die by the sword in his own land
questions.explanation: God promised that the Assyrian king would fall by the sword in his own land (Isaiah 37:7).

questions.question: What did Hezekiah do with the letter from Sennacherib?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah received the letter and spread it before the LORD (Isaiah 37:14).

questions.question: What does the term 'remnant' refer to in the context of Isaiah 37:31?
questions.explanation: The 'remnant' refers to those from the house of Judah who would escape and survive (Isaiah 37:31).

questions.question: What was the sign given to Hezekiah regarding the future harvests?
options: They would have to import food
They would eat from what grows of itself for two years
questions.correctAnswer: They would eat from what grows of itself for two years
questions.explanation: The sign indicated that they would eat from what grows of itself in the first two years before they could sow and reap (Isaiah 37:30).

questions.question: According to Isaiah 37:35, why will God defend the city of Jerusalem?
options: For the glory of the people
For mine own sake and for my servant David's sake
questions.correctAnswer: For mine own sake and for my servant David's sake
questions.explanation: God states that He will defend the city for His own sake and for David's sake (Isaiah 37:35).

questions.question: How many Assyrians did the angel of the LORD smite in their camp?
questions.explanation: The angel of the LORD smote 185,000 Assyrians in their camp (Isaiah 37:36).

questions.question: What ultimately happened to Sennacherib after the defeat of the Assyrians?
questions.explanation: After the defeat, Sennacherib king of Assyria departed and returned to Nineveh (Isaiah 37:37).

questions.question: True or False: Hezekiah prayed to the LORD after receiving the distressing letter.
questions.explanation: Hezekiah prayed to the LORD after receiving the letter from Sennacherib (Isaiah 37:15).

questions.question: True or False: The gods of the nations were able to save them from the Assyrians according to Hezekiah.
questions.explanation: Hezekiah recognized that the gods of the nations were not able to save them, as they were mere works of men's hands (Isaiah 37:19).

questions.question: What literary device is used in Isaiah 37:28 regarding God's knowledge of the Assyrian king's actions?
questions.explanation: The verse uses parallelism by emphasizing God's comprehensive knowledge of the Assyrian king's abode and actions (Isaiah 37:28).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God defending His people as seen in Isaiah 37?
questions.explanation: Romans 8:31 echoes the theme of God being for His people, paralleling God's promise to defend Jerusalem in Isaiah 37:35.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 37 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 37 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What action did King Hezekiah take upon hearing the news from Assyria?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah rent his clothes as a sign of mourning and distress upon hearing the news, as stated in Isaiah 37:1.

questions.question: Who did Hezekiah send to Isaiah the prophet?
options: Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests
questions.correctAnswer: Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests
questions.explanation: Hezekiah sent Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests to Isaiah, as recorded in Isaiah 37:2.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah express about the day he was facing?
options: A day of trouble and rebuke
questions.correctAnswer: A day of trouble and rebuke
questions.explanation: Hezekiah described the day as one of trouble and rebuke, indicating the serious nature of the threats against Judah, as seen in Isaiah 37:3.

questions.question: What did Isaiah tell Hezekiah not to be afraid of?
questions.explanation: Isaiah instructed Hezekiah not to be afraid of the blasphemous words of Rabshakeh, as stated in Isaiah 37:6.

questions.question: What promise did God give regarding the king of Assyria?
options: He will return to his own land
He will become a servant of Hezekiah
He will make peace with Judah
questions.correctAnswer: He will return to his own land
questions.explanation: God promised that He would cause the king of Assyria to hear a rumor and return to his own land, as declared in Isaiah 37:7.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah do with the letter from the king of Assyria?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah received the letter, read it, and then prayed to the LORD, as described in Isaiah 37:14-15.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is emphasized in Hezekiah's prayer?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah acknowledges God's sovereignty over all kingdoms of the earth in his prayer, particularly in Isaiah 37:16.

questions.question: What did God reveal about the fate of the Assyrian king?
options: He will be defeated by the Israelites
He shall not come into this city
questions.correctAnswer: He shall not come into this city
questions.explanation: God declared that the king of Assyria would not enter Jerusalem, as stated in Isaiah 37:33.

questions.question: What sign did God give regarding the future of Judah?
options: They will eat what grows of itself
They will be taken into captivity
questions.correctAnswer: They will eat what grows of itself
questions.explanation: God provided a sign that Judah would eat what grows of itself for two years, as noted in Isaiah 37:30.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 37:36 reveal about God's power over the Assyrians?
options: God sent an angel to smite them
questions.correctAnswer: God sent an angel to smite them
questions.explanation: The verse states that the angel of the LORD smote a great number of Assyrians, showcasing God's power, as recorded in Isaiah 37:36.

questions.question: What theological theme is evident in the way God defends Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: God's defense of Jerusalem underscores His commitment to His covenant with His people, as He saves it for His own sake and for David's sake in Isaiah 37:35.

questions.question: Which aspect of God's nature is highlighted by His response to Sennacherib's blasphemies?
questions.explanation: God's response to the blasphemies of Sennacherib highlights His wrath against those who oppose Him, as seen in Isaiah 37:23.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that God is unable to protect His people from foreign powers. What does Isaiah 37:21-22 actually teach?
options: God is indifferent to His people's plight
God will not intervene in human affairs
God actively defends His people against their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: God actively defends His people against their enemies
questions.explanation: Isaiah 37:21-22 reveals that God actively defends His people, indicating His power and care for Jerusalem, contrary to the skeptics' claims.

questions.question: How does the chapter reflect the theme of divine sovereignty in history?
options: By showing that nations rise and fall without God's knowledge
By demonstrating that God controls the outcomes of nations
By indicating that human decisions are irrelevant
By illustrating that victory is based on military strength
questions.correctAnswer: By demonstrating that God controls the outcomes of nations
questions.explanation: The events involving Hezekiah, Assyria, and God's intervention show that God is sovereign over the affairs of nations, particularly in Isaiah 37:7 and 37:36.

questions.question: What do verses 19-20 teach about the nature of false gods?
options: They are powerful and should be feared
They are mere creations of human hands
They are more reliable than the God of Israel
They can provide protection against enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They are mere creations of human hands
questions.explanation: Isaiah 37:19-20 emphasizes that the gods of the nations are not true deities but the work of men's hands, underscoring their impotence compared to the living God.
